newsitem.title: GREECE: Greek parliament approves abolition of tax breaks.
newsitem.headline: Greek parliament approves abolition of tax breaks.

text.p: The Greek parliament approved on Thursday a controversial bill abolishing tax breaks for thousands of workers and imposing taxes on government debt paper.
The new law will go into effect next Tuesday after being published in the Government Gazette, parliament officials told Reuters.
The tough law applies a 7.5 percent tax on interest earned from government bonds and Treasury bills.
The government estimates that the new law would yield some 300 billion drachmas this year.
The bill was opposed by a wide range of labour unions and workers staged nationwide demonstrations and work stoppages in late December and January.

Socialist Prime Minister Costas Simitis has said the new taxes were necessary to cut towering public debts and bring the country's economy in line with those of its European Union partners. -Margarita Sotiropoulou, Athens Newsroom, +301 3311812-4
